boundary.description: Playwright drives the real Angular SPA (built with the e2e configuration, enableE2eTools on) at E2E_APP_URL against a real TMI server at E2E_API_URL with its real Postgres and Redis. Seed data is provisioned out-of-band and idempotently by `make e2e-seed` in the sibling tmi repo; identity comes from the server's built-in 'tmi' test OAuth provider via login_hint (requires the server's dev/test build_mode). Where a scenario claims persistence, it additionally reads state back through an independent REST call using the page's authenticated session rather than re-reading the page it just wrote.
boundary.rationale: This is the only boundary the repo owns end to end, and it is the one already built out: a four-project Playwright layout with flows/page-objects/dialog-objects, delete-via-api teardown, and server-side seeding. It is also the only boundary at which the product's authorization model is observable, which is where most of the untested risk sits. Everything below it — calculator math, input-validation permutations, SurveyJS's own visibleIf engine, X6 rendering — is disqualified by the tier rule and pushed down to Vitest.
real: tmi-ux SPA (e2e build, served by ng serve)
Redis (via the server, edit locks and pending links)
the server's built-in 'tmi' test OAuth provider
stubbed: external OAuth identity providers (Google, GitHub, Microsoft) — the 'tmi' test provider stands in
Google Drive / Google Picker and the Microsoft file picker — left to the human-attended, opt-in google-drive-live project
webhook delivery and any server egress — not observable from the browser

scenarios.boundary: browser against live SPA + live TMI API + live WebSocket

preconditions.state: an active session with owner and a writer participant
preconditions.via: S-J8-1 helpers with a writer grant
preconditions.assert_established: both are listed as participants
preconditions.rationale: Concurrency requires two connected writers.

steps: Both participants add a distinct node at nearly the same time
Both move a shared node
Wait for convergence
Both re-read the diagram via API
assertions: both nodes exist for both participants after convergence
the persisted diagram contains both nodes exactly once
if an operation is rejected, a state_correction/resync brings the client back in line (R-W09-15)
negative_assertions: no duplicate cells
no participant is left with a diverged canvas after the polling budget

cleanup: end session, delete diagram and TM

determinism_controls: assert on convergence within a bounded budget, never on interleaving order
compare persisted cell sets rather than screenshots

placement.naming: Collaboration > concurrent edits converge

open_assumptions: true simultaneity is not achievable from one runner; this tests near-simultaneous ordering, which is the realistic seam
server conflict resolution is observable to the client as documented

scenarios.title: Publishing offers a survey at intake and deactivating withdraws it
scenarios.boundary: browser against live SPA + live TMI API

preconditions.state: a run-owned draft survey
preconditions.via: admin creates a small survey in the template builder without publishing
preconditions.assert_established: the survey exists with a non-published status
preconditions.rationale: The status transition is the seam; the survey must start unpublished.

steps: Admin publishes the survey
User opens /intake
Admin deactivates it
User reloads /intake
Admin archives it
assertions: after publish, the user is offered the survey by name at /intake
after deactivate, the survey is absent from /intake for the user
each status change is confirmed by the survey's API payload, not only by an admin list chip
negative_assertions: the deactivated survey is not merely reordered but genuinely absent
other published surveys remain offered

cleanup: delete the run survey; assert no clone of a seeded fixture was left behind

determinism_controls: assert status from the API payload — the /active/i chip matched 'Inactive' in the existing test
never clone or mutate the seeded Kitchen Sink survey

placement.naming: Survey publication > publish offers and deactivate withdraws

open_assumptions: intake visibility follows status without a caching delay

scenarios.title: A non-admin manages a team and project and filters the dashboard by them
scenarios.boundary: browser against live SPA + live TMI API

preconditions.state: authenticated as test-user (not admin)
preconditions.assert_established: on an authenticated route
preconditions.rationale: The existing suites run this surface as test-admin, which erases the API-scoping dimension S-R-S04-02 describes.

steps: Create a team via /teams, add a member and a responsible party, add metadata
Create a project via /projects associated with that team
Create a TM and link it to the project
On /dashboard, filter by that project
Reload the filtered URL
assertions: each write is confirmed by reopening the dialog and by an independent API read
the filtered dashboard shows the linked TM
the filter state is reflected in the URL and reproduced on reload (R-W8-5)
the /teams page offers no delete action for a non-admin (R-S04-01)
negative_assertions: a second, unlinked TM created in the same run is absent from the filtered results — the assertion the existing filter tests omit
no team or project owned by another user appears

cleanup: delete the TMs, project, and team (as admin if a non-admin cannot delete), asserting each

determinism_controls: a control TM that must be absent, so the filter assertion cannot hold before the filter is applied
no waitForTimeout around filter application — wait on the list request
fixtures_to_reuse: TeamFlow, ProjectFlow, DashboardFilterFlow, TeamsPage, ProjectsPage, CreateTeamDialog, CreateProjectDialog
new_helpers_needed: waitForFilteredList(page) resolving on the list response

placement.naming: Teams and projects > non-admin CRUD and dashboard filtering

open_assumptions: a non-admin can create teams and projects; if the API scopes creation to admins, the scenario becomes a denial test instead and that is itself the finding

scenarios.title: Timmy chat is scoped to the threat model and honors timmy_enabled
scenarios.boundary: browser against live SPA + live TMI API (LLM-backed endpoint)

preconditions.state: a TM with two notes, one with timmy_enabled false
preconditions.via: create TM + two notes, toggling the flag on one
preconditions.assert_established: the notes' API payloads report the expected timmy_enabled values
preconditions.rationale: The flag's effect on retrieval scope is the requirement under test.

steps: Open the Timmy chat from the TM page
Ask a question whose answer would require the excluded note's content
Ask a question answerable from the included note
Reload and reopen the session
assertions: a chat session is created scoped to this TM
the response grounded in the included note references its content
the excluded note's distinctive content does not appear in the response or the cited sources
the session is resumable after reload
negative_assertions: no content from another threat model appears in the response

cleanup: delete the chat session if the API allows, then the TM and notes

determinism_controls: assert on source attribution / absence of a distinctive token rather than on LLM prose
avoid asserting exact response wording
new_helpers_needed: ChatPage page object and a TimmyFlow

placement.naming: Timmy > chat is TM-scoped and respects timmy_enabled

open_assumptions: the e2e server has LLM credentials or a deterministic canned mode; without one this scenario cannot run and should be marked skipped-with-reason rather than deleted
the wiki states the Timmy frontend is not yet implemented while client code exists under pages/chat — the scenario may need to wait on the feature

scenarios.title: Peer-authored markdown cannot execute script on any render surface
scenarios.boundary: browser against live SPA + live TMI API

preconditions.state: a TM shared writer-to-writer between two users so one can persist markdown the other renders
preconditions.via: owner creates a TM and grants writer to test-reviewer
preconditions.assert_established: both can write; the authorization payload lists writer
preconditions.rationale: The threat requires an authenticated attacker persisting content a victim later renders — the exact shape TRIAGE.md's f001 describes.

steps: As the attacker, persist hostile markdown into a TM note, a triage note, and a chat message: a javascript: link, a quote-breaking title attribute, an onerror image, and a data: URI
As the victim, open each rendering surface
Register a page-level error/dialog listener and a window-level flag before each navigation
Inspect the rendered anchors' href/src attributes
assertions: no script executed on any surface (no dialog, no injected global, no console-visible execution marker)
rendered anchor href values are either stripped or a safe scheme; no javascript: or data: href reaches the DOM
the visible text is preserved (sanitization did not blank the content)
negative_assertions: no onerror/onload attribute survives in the rendered DOM
no attribute-boundary escape: the title attribute did not become new markup

cleanup: delete the notes, chat messages, and TM

determinism_controls: use an execution flag on window rather than expecting a dialog (dialogs block the driver)
assert on the DOM attribute values, not on a screenshot
new_helpers_needed: assertNoScriptExecution(page) installing and checking the flag

placement.naming: Markdown sanitization > hostile content cannot execute on any surface

open_assumptions: TRIAGE.md f001 is still unfixed; if it has been fixed this scenario is the regression guard, and if not it will fail on first run — which is the point

scenarios.title: Admin routes reject service-account tokens and non-admins, and server-controlled fields stay immutable
scenarios.boundary: browser against live SPA + live TMI API

preconditions.state: a client-credentials token owned by an admin user
preconditions.via: admin creates client credentials in User Preferences, then exchanges them for a CCG token
preconditions.assert_established: the token exchange returns an access token
preconditions.rationale: R-W10-2 is specifically about a CCG token owned by an administrator; only composing it through the real credential flow produces a token the server will accept as a service account.

preconditions.state: a TM owned by test-user
preconditions.assert_established: GET returns 200 with created_at recorded
preconditions.rationale: Immutability needs a real record with server-set fields.

steps: Call each /admin API route with the CCG token
Call one /admin route with test-user's interactive session
Navigate test-user to /admin in the browser
PATCH the TM attempting to change created_at, id, and created_by
assertions: every /admin route returns 403 for the CCG token (R-W10-2)
the /admin route returns 403 for the non-admin interactive session
the browser navigation lands on a specific denial destination and the Admin nav link is absent for test-user (R-W8-3)
the immutable-field PATCH is rejected or ignored, and a follow-up GET shows created_at, id, and created_by unchanged (R-W09-9)
negative_assertions: no admin route returned 200 to the service-account token
no server-controlled field changed value

cleanup: revoke the client credential, delete the TM

determinism_controls: enumerate admin routes from a single table so a new admin route is covered by construction
assert exact status codes, not merely a redirect
new_helpers_needed: mintServiceAccountToken(adminPage) returning a CCG access token

placement.naming: AuthZ boundaries > service accounts and non-admins are denied; server fields immutable

open_assumptions: client-credential creation is available to the seeded admin in the e2e environment
the server rejects rather than silently ignoring immutable-field PATCHes; if it ignores, the read-back assertion carries the test
